qt: to the Commission Nikolaj Villumsen (The Left) Subject:

Last year, the Commission issued a communication on an ‘EU Action Plan1: Protecting and restoring marine ecosystems for sustainable and resilient fisheries’. In it, inter alia, the Commission calls on Member States, by the end of March 2024, to adopt national measures or, where appropriate, propose joint recommendations to the regional groups to prohibit mobile bottom fishing in marine protected areas which are Natura 2000 sites designated under the Habitats Directive that protect the seabed and marine species (COM(2023) 102, 21.2.2023, p. 11). 1.

Will the Commission take new initiatives to promote protection of Natura 2000 areas from bottom fishing, such as beam trawling, especially in the light of the objective of phasing out the use of bottom-contact gear in protected areas?
Does the Commission regard it as satisfactory and commensurate with biodiversity safeguarding that it is taking so many years to protect Natura 2000 areas from bottom fishing?
at: (English version) to the Commission Nikolaj Villumsen (The Left) (1 March 2024) Subject: EU action plan and bottom fishing Last year, the Commission issued a communication on an ‘EU Action Plan (1): Protecting and restoring marine ecosystems for sustainable and resilient fisheries’. In it, inter alia, the Commission calls on Member States, by the end of March 2024, to adopt national measures or, where appropriate, propose joint recommendations to the regional groups to prohibit mobile bottom fishing in marine protected areas which are Natura 2000 sites designated under the Habitats Directive that protect the seabed and marine species (COM(2023) 102, 21.2.2023, p. 11). 1. Will the Commission take new initiatives to promote protection of Natura 2000 areas from bottom fishing, such as beam trawling, especially in the light of the objective of phasing out the use of bottom-contact gear in protected areas? 2. Does the Commission regard it as satisfactory and commensurate with biodiversity safeguarding that it is taking so many years to protect Natura 2000 areas from bottom fishing? (3 May 2024) 1. The Marine Action Plan is part of the Fisheries and Ocean package adopted by the Commission in February 2023 which brings together different aspects of the EU’s policy on fisheries and the environment and looks at the future in which marine biodiversity is preserved and fisheries continues to grow in resilience and sustainability. Within that context, what the action plan is advocating for is a gradual transition to less damage to the seabed, especially in the most sensitive marine areas. The climate and biodiversity crisis calls for urgent action and the Commission continues to urge Member States to make full use of the tools under the regionalised common fisheries policy to develop appropriate solutions regionally. 2. In line with the commitments of the EU Biodiversity Strategy and the Marine Action Plan, the Commission will continue to work with Member States to step up efforts to ensure full implementation of obligations under the Birds (2) and Habitats (3) Directives, within and outside Natura 2000. The Commission has ongoing infringements against Member States for their failure to establish site-specific conservation objectives and measures for Natura 2000 sites. Among them, 14 infringements concern coastal Member States and the majority cover marine sites.
